description: I am building AstroLab: an interactive React-based Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer where kids balance power, life support, and radiation using real NASA data. I have a strong full-stack UI/UX background but am currently working solo. I am looking for teammates with skills in React, game mechanics, or data visualization to help me build the MVP this weekend. Let's win this!
summary: AstroLab is an interactive, open-source deep space outpost simulator designed to teach children ages 7–12 the critical engineering trade-offs of space exploration. Players manage a lunar or Martian outpost, balancing competing demands such as life support, radiation shielding, power budgeting, and food production. Grounded in real NASA data from the Space Weather Database (DONKI) and the Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), AstroLab turns genuine mission constraints into engaging gameplay mechanics. Every decision carries a resource cost, demonstrating how NASA mission planners navigate survival in deep space. By bridging the gap between abstract space facts and hands-on resource management, AstroLab makes complex scientific decision-making tangible, accessible, and fun for young learners.
details:
• What it does & how it works: AstroLab is a web-based resource-management game where players take on the role of a mission commander. They are presented with simulated daily scenarios that require allocating limited resources. For example, players might have to trade oxygen reserves for an extra research opportunity, or reinforce shielding against an impending solar event at the cost of the outpost's power supply.
  • Benefits & intended impact: The game translates abstract space education into interactive, consequence-based learning. Instead of simply memorizing facts, young players learn by experiencing the actual decision-making logic behind a deep space mission, fostering critical thinking and genuine STEM engagement.
  • Tools used: Built as a responsive web application utilizing React, Next.js, and Tailwind CSS, allowing for a low-barrier, browser-playable experience with no downloads or account registration required.
  • Creativity & considerations: We intentionally avoided designing "safe" choices. Every decision in AstroLab involves a genuine trade-off, mirroring real mission planning. We also prioritized mechanical accuracy and visual simplicity over overwhelming UI, focusing on three core resources to keep the cognitive load appropriate for the 7–12 age bracket.
dataRefs: Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI)
